gloss: business rival; trade competitor; commercial rival

definitions.gloss: business rival; trade competitor; commercial rival
definitions.explanation: A person or business that competes directly in the same trade or market. Carries a sense of personal rivalry, not just impersonal market competition.

examples.japanese: あの{店|みせ}はうちの{商売仇|しょうばいがたき}だ。
examples.english: That shop is our business rival.

examples.japanese: {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}の{動向|どうこう}には{常|つね}に{注意|ちゅうい}している。
examples.english: I always keep an eye on the activities of our business rivals.

examples.japanese: {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}だった{二人|ふたり}が{協力|きょうりょく}して{新|あたら}しい{事業|じぎょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The two, who had been business rivals, joined forces to start a new venture.

notes:
A compound of {商売|しょうばい} (business, trade) and {仇|がたき} (rival, enemy). The word has a personal, somewhat old-fashioned flavor — it implies not just competition but a sense of rivalry between specific people or shops in the same trade.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}になる: to become business rivals
- {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}を{意識|いしき}する: to be conscious of one's business rival
- {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}の{店|みせ}: a rival shop
- {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}に{負|ま}けない: to not lose to one's business rival

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {競合|きょうごう}: competitor, competing — a modern, neutral business term for market competition; {商売仇|しょうばいがたき} is more personal and vivid
- ライバル: rival — the English loanword, used broadly in sports, business, and personal contexts
- {競争相手|きょうそうあいて}: competitor — a neutral term for any competitor; lacks the personal edge of {商売仇|しょうばいがたき}

REGISTER:
Somewhat old-fashioned and literary. Evokes the image of traditional shopkeepers or small business owners competing on the same street. In modern corporate contexts, {競合|きょうごう} or {競争相手|きょうそうあいて} is more common.
